segments.source: SparseSolve(_:_:_:_:)
**Framework**: Accelerate **Kind**: func
Solve `AX=B` using the specified iterative method for complex double values.

segments.source: Parameters
`method`: (Input) Iterative method specification, eg return value of `SparseConjugateGradient()`.
segments.ko: `method`: (Input) Iterative method specification, eg return value of `SparseConjugateGradient()`.

segments.source: `A`: (Input) The matrix `A` to solve the system for. Only used for multiplication by `A` or `A^T`.
segments.ko: `A`: (Input) The matrix `A` to solve the system for. Only used for multiplication by `A` or `A^T`.

segments.source: `B`: The right-hand sides `B` to solve for. If `A` has dimension `m x n`, then `B` must have dimension `m x nrhs`, where `nrhs` is the number of right-hand sides to find solutions for.
segments.ko: `B`: The right-hand sides `B` to solve for. If `A` has dimension `m x n`, then `B` must have dimension `m x nrhs`, where `nrhs` is the number of right-hand sides to find solutions for.

segments.source: `X`: On entry, initial guess for solution, on return the solution. If A has dimension `m x n`, and `B` has dimension `m x nrhs`, then `X` must have dimension `n x nrhs`. If no good initial estimate is available, user should set the initial guess to be the zero vector.
segments.ko: `X`: On entry, initial guess for solution, on return the solution. If A has dimension `m x n`, and `B` has dimension `m x nrhs`, then `X` must have dimension `n x nrhs`. If no good initial estimate is available, user should set the initial guess to be the zero vector.
